concerns.text: FR-001 defaults to MDS coordinates derived from the adjacency matrix when real coordinates are missing. MDS coordinates are a deterministic function of topology, so 'geographic proximity' becomes a re-encoding of topological distance — the spatial model then partially restates the topology-only baseline, and the research question ('empirically measured geographic proximity') is no longer being tested. The spec must restrict the MDS fallback to a clearly-labeled synthetic control condition, not a substitute for the empirical claim.

Paired t-tests across 50 Monte Carlo runs are mis-specified: independent stochastic simulations have no natural pairing (run index is arbitrary), so 'paired' is unjustified; use two-sample tests on the run distributions. Additionally, final-size/peak-infection distributions near threshold are strongly skewed/bimodal, violating t-test normality; a permutation or rank-based test against the 100-run null distribution (FR-004) would be the appropriate comparison.

The epidemic threshold ('critical β') is treated as a per-run observable, but no estimation procedure is specified (grid interpolation? crossing of a prevalence criterion?), and the edge case admits it may be undefined in many runs. A t-test on thresholds requires a defined estimator and a policy for undefined values beyond 'report undefined' — the statistical comparison of thresholds (SC-001) is currently not well-defined.

'resulting in a lower peak infection rate compared to the λ=0 run' is true by construction (β_ij = β_0·e^{-λd} ≤ β_0 for every edge), so it cannot fail and is not an empirical finding. Reword to a non-trivial check, e.g. that the reduction exceeds what randomized coordinates produce, or quantify the reduction relative to the null model.
